title: Optical cross-check of the harvest map

reflectance.rule: reflectance = DN * 0.0001, minus 0.1 only where earthsearch:boa_offset_applied is false on a processing baseline of 04.00 or later; the offset -0.1 that the assets' raster:bands list is not used (where the catalog says the offset is already removed it would remove it twice)

offset_check.rule: a guard, not a definition: a scene taken as offset-free stops the run when under min_share of its vegetation pixels have a red value below red_dn_below; not checked with fewer than min_pixels vegetation pixels

settings.split_granules: the granules of one tile and date are mosaicked only when they share s2:datatake_id and have distinct s2:datastrip_id values with distinct sensing starts; otherwise the run stops

bootstrap.rng: numpy.random.default_rng(20261115), a fresh generator for each interval

limits: An optical index sees green, not stems: ripening, weeds, a second crop and smoke haze all move it.
A 100 m cell holds several fields.
Cloud and smoke leave gaps, so "cut by day D" depends on which dates are usable.
Sentinel-2 passes at about 11:00 local time and NISAR at 05:43, days apart.
The comparison is made afterwards, like the fire check.
The marker decision (HV) is not reopened by this: it was made by a rule fixed beforehand. The numbers are reported for HH and HV without recommending a change.
T_pooled separates green from not green; ripening rice loses green before it is cut, so this threshold calls some standing, ripe rice "cut".
